Enable eval clone access to stackhawk-research

This sets up a read-only GitHub App so the agent-skills CI evals can clone repos from stackhawk-research. You need admin/owner on both stackhawk-research and stackhawk/agent-skills — the whole flow below is done by one person. Budget ~5 minutes.

Before you start: make sure this browser is signed into GitHub as your stackhawk-research owner account. The button below only pre-fills GitHub's app form — nothing is created until you confirm on GitHub's own page.

Step 1. Create the GitHub App

Click to open GitHub's app-creation flow, pre-filled with the correct name, permissions (contents: read, metadata: read), no webhooks, private:

Review the pre-filled form and click GitHub's Create GitHub App button at the bottom. GitHub creates the app and returns you to the org's GitHub Apps list (the ?code=… in the URL is harmless — ignore it). Click into the new StackHawk Research Repo Reader app to open its settings.

Step 2. Grab the App ID and a private key

  1. Near the top of the app settings page, copy the App ID (a number). Keep it handy.
  2. Scroll to Private keys → click Generate a private key. A .pem file downloads. Keep it handy (you'll paste its contents in Step 4).

Step 3. Install the App on all repos

  1. In the app's left sidebar, click Install App.
  2. Click Install next to stackhawk-research.
  3. Choose All repositories — the App stays read-only (contents: read), and this way any repo we add as an eval target later works with no re-install.
  4. Click Install.

Step 4. Add two secrets to stackhawk/agent-skills

The App lives in stackhawk-research, but the credentials that mint its tokens are stored in the consumer repo's Actions secrets. Open:

github.com → stackhawk/agent-skills → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret

Direct link: github.com/stackhawk/agent-skills/settings/secrets/actions

Add these two secrets exact names:

Secret nameValue to paste
RESEARCH_APP_ID The App ID number from Step 2 (digits only, e.g. 1234567).
RESEARCH_APP_PRIVATE_KEY The entire contents of the .pem from Step 2 — open it in a text editor and paste everything, including the -----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY----- and -----END RSA PRIVATE KEY----- lines.
Names must match exactly — the workflow reads secrets.RESEARCH_APP_ID and secrets.RESEARCH_APP_PRIVATE_KEY. Case-sensitive. No surrounding quotes.

Done

That's it. Let the person driving PR #69 know both secrets are set — they'll dispatch the eval workflow and confirm the four discovery repos clone and run. You can delete the downloaded .pem afterward; GitHub keeps the key, and you can generate a new one anytime.
